claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch on a narrow aggregate-readiness basis despite a known 1.5-point miss in a named regulated-customer segment and an open legal review about whether that gap must be disclosed.
specific_concerns: The policy makes weaknesses material when they affect a contractual customer segment or named launch use case, and the affected health-plan benefits support segment is named in a regulated-customer pilot order form.
The release policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
There is admissible evidence of an open legal ticket on whether disclosure is required, but no admissible evidence of a final legal determination, actual disclosure, or approved risk acceptance.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness, but they do not satisfy the separate disclosure predicate for a material limitation.
The product note calling the segment non-core does not resolve materiality under the stated policy context.
unsupported_claims: The claim that certification is supportable now is not adequately supported because the required disclosure-or-approved-risk-acceptance condition is unresolved.
Any implication that preserving the issue in the record is sufficient compliance is unsupported absent evidence of actual disclosure or approved risk acceptance before launch.
evidence_requests: Provide the final legal determination on whether the named segment gap must be disclosed.
Provide the launch disclosure or model-card text that discloses the segment-specific limitation, if it exists.
Provide approved risk-acceptance documentation covering the named segment gap before launch.
Provide the relevant customer commitment or pilot order-form language to confirm scope of the named use case.
decision_criteria: If admissible evidence shows the material limitation was disclosed before launch, the action could move toward compliant_with_caveats or compliant depending on completeness.
If admissible evidence shows an approved pre-launch risk acceptance covering this exact gap, the action could move toward compliant_with_caveats.
If neither disclosure nor approved risk acceptance exists, certifying the model for launch remains noncompliant under the stated policy.
Operational readiness evidence alone is insufficient where a separate material-disclosure requirement applies.
